title: Larkview HealthTech onboarding & risk handoff
summary: Kickoff to align on onboarding timeline, security controls, and pilot success criteria. Redwood AE and SE walked through network architecture options (hosted vs private/VPC vs on-prem container), confirmed security questionnaire next steps, and scoped a two-week pilot focusing on ingest and inference latency targets. Action items assigned for topology diagram, credentials handoff, and a small benchmark plan.
action_items: Priya Nair: Share VPC peering diagram and AWS account IDs by 2026-04-06
Ethan Cole: Draft pilot benchmark script and sample prompt set by 2026-04-05
Maya Thompson: Send pricing ballpark and pilot contract template by 2026-04-04
Samir Patel: Provide current infra telemetry (p95 latency, token counts) by 2026-04-07
Marta Ivanova: Confirm KMS provider and compliance contacts by 2026-04-09
next_steps: Schedule technical lunch-and-learn for dev team (Ethan + Samir) next week
Redwood to run a 1-hour benchmark in Larkview staging with sample models
Customer to complete security questionnaire and provide network details
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 1:02
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Priya (CTO), Daniel (Head of ML), Samir (DevOps), Olivia (Product), Marta (Security)

Summary (auto): Align on onboarding plan, pick deployment mode, list security deliverables.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, welcome, thanks for making the time. Quick intros, I'll kick it off — I'm Maya Thompson, account lead for Larkview.
[00:07] Priya: Hi Maya, Priya here. Thanks, excited to finally get this moving.
[00:10] Daniel: Daniel Ruiz, head of ML — we'll be running the NLU features and some rerankers.
[00:14] Samir: Samir, DevOps. I'll own the infra bits.
[00:16] Olivia: Olivia, product, hi.
[00:18] Marta: Marta, security/compliance.
[00:21] Ethan: Ethan Cole, solutions engineer at Redwood. I'll run the benchmarks and the technical runbook.
[00:24] Jordan: Jordan Lee, your customer success manager. I'll make sure milestones get tracked.

[00:30] Maya: Great. Agenda: 1) run through your priorities and success criteria for the pilot, 2) discuss the deployment options and recommended architecture, 3) security and compliance handoffs, and 4) next steps / timeline. Sound good?
[00:41] Priya: Sounds good. High level — we want predictable latency for our chat assistant (p95 under 450ms ideally) and we need data residency in us-east-1. Also, we have strict PHI-ish rules, so encryption and audit logs are required.
[00:56] Maya: Understood. Redwood has a few ways to do this — we can do hosted with strict tenancy, Dedicated pool, or Private VPC/control plane. Ethan, quick summary of tradeoffs?
[01:06] Ethan: Yep. Hosted is fastest to stand up but you'll be on shared infra, we do tenant isolation and SOC controls but for PHI we usually recommend Private — either VPC-hosted control plane or on-prem depending on your compliance posture. Dedicated gives predictability for throughput but still managed by us. For latency, caching + KV cache (we sometimes see notes where KV got transcribed as K V cash) and batching settings will be key.
[01:33] Daniel: If we go private VPC, what's the timeline to get the control plane talking? We're trying to start the pilot in two weeks.
[01:39] Ethan: Two weeks is tight but doable for VPC peering if network team is responsive. On-prem would take longer. For the pilot we often start with a hosted sandbox while we parallel the VPC peering setup — that gets you an immediate surface for functional tests and then we failover traffic to the private route once peering is live.
[02:00] Samir: I want to understand peering vs transit gateway options. We use TGW across accounts. We'll need a diagram of the ports and inbound/outbound paths.
[02:08] Maya: We'll share a network topology doc. Priya, can you surface the AWS account IDs and TGW info?
[02:13] Priya: Yes, we can. I'll get that to you.
[02:16] Marta: On security, we need to verify KMS integration and whether Redwood keys or customer-managed KMS will be used. Also SAML SSO and RBAC for the console access.
[02:28] Jordan: We have SSO integrations — we support SAML and OIDC, RBAC roles can map to your groups.
[02:33] Marta: Also audit logs retention — do you retain API-level logs for 13 months?
[02:37] Ethan: Default retention is 90 days for the hosted plan; we can offer extended retention as an add-on or through the Private deployment where logs are pushed to your SIEM. We'll capture the compliance package details and send them over.
[02:52] Olivia: For the pilot scope, we want 2 use cases: chat assistant for support triage and a reranker for search results. Success = precision lift on reranker + latency under 450ms for chat. Also cost per 1k interactions should be within our projected budget.
[03:08] Maya: Good — we'll define metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens per session, cost per 1k). Ethan will propose a benchmark script.
[03:16] Ethan: I'll create a simple harness that runs your prompt set against two model variants — one quantized low-latency, one higher-quality — to show tradeoffs. Also will measure cold-start and cache-warm p95.
[03:27] Daniel: For reranker, we have a small internal model — are you able to host custom models in the pod?
[03:31] Ethan: Yes, we can host customer models if they meet size/format requirements. We'll need the model artifact and a brief spec. For the pilot it's easiest to test with our verified catalog models and then swap in your artifact for a second stage.
[03:43] Priya: About data flow — we want to avoid sending raw PII back to external logs. Is there an option to redact before logs leave the VPC?
[03:51] Ethan: On Private, logs can be retained entirely inside your network. For hosted, we offer masking hooks and sampling controls, but full-on redaction is easier to guarantee with VPC/private. We'll put a recommended practice doc together.
[04:06] Samir: On ingress, are there any agent dependencies? We run EKS and have a service mesh.
[04:11] Ethan: No heavy agents — we use standard TLS endpoints. For VPC peering there's a small NAT/proxy configuration for outbound if you want model fetching to go through your proxy. It all goes in the runbook.
[04:22] Maya: Ok timeline: We propose start pilot this coming Monday (2026-04-06). Jordan will coordinate. Ethan will run an initial benchmark in staging on Friday and share results. Priya/Samir to share network and account details by Wednesday. Marta to confirm KMS/SOC2 questions by end of next week.
[04:40] Priya: Monday is ambitious but we'll aim for it, Samir will prioritize.
[04:44] Samir: Ok.
[04:46] Olivia: A question on rollouts: if we see quality regressions, do we have an auto rollback?
[04:50] Ethan: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a previous model variant. Our console shows per-route metrics and will mark a failed rollout if latency or error rate crosses thresholds.
[04:59] Daniel: Great — can we capture tokenization parity? We use a custom tokenizer for the reranker.
[05:04] Ethan: We'll need a tokenizer spec; tokenization differences can cause token accounting differences which affect cost. We'll add that to the checklist.
[05:11] Jordan: Quick note — pricing for pilot: we usually provide a short-term credit and then a usage estimate. Maya will send a ballpark and a pilot contract.
[05:19] Maya: Yep I'll send that today.
[05:22] Priya: Anything else on compliance side? Marta?
[05:24] Marta: Please send SOC2, ISO27001, and the pen test summary. Also I'd like the list of sub-processors.
[05:31] Maya: We'll attach the compliance pack.
[05:33] Ethan: For benchmarks, do you have representative prompt sets?
[05:36] Daniel: Yes, I'll share a 200-sample prompt set — mixing short chat prompts and long context examples.
[05:42] Ethan: Perfect. I'll run them at different concurrency levels to surface p95 at realistic load.
[05:48] Samir: On cost optimization, what about quantization and batching tradeoffs?
[05:52] Ethan: We'll show configurations. Quantized model + aggressive batching reduces cost but increases latency variance; with prefix caching you can keep p95 low. We'll include a recommended config.
[06:04] Olivia: Who will be our day-to-day contacts?
[06:07] Maya: Maya for contract/pricing, Jordan for success milestones, Ethan for tech. We'll make an internal contact sheet.
[06:12] Priya: Ok sounds good.
[06:14] Maya: Quick recap of next steps — Priya share network & account IDs by 2026-04-06; Samir provide telemetry; Marta provide KMS and compliance priorities; Ethan draft benchmark and run Friday; Maya send pilot contract and pricing by 2026-04-04; Jordan will schedule the dev lunch-and-learn.
[06:34] Daniel: One last thing — any special firewall ports?
[06:36] Ethan: We'll circulate a small table but typically HTTPS outbound to our endpoint, and if you're doing peering, no public egress is required.
[06:44] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward.
[06:46] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and the action-item list.
[06:50] Marta: Thanks.
[06:52] Jordan: Bye all.

End of meeting.

References shared during call:
- "Pilot checklist" doc (link in meeting notes)
- Compliance pack (SOC2/ISO) to be attached by Maya
- Benchmark harness template (Ethan will provide GitHub gist)
